The companion canonical Weber work to *Economy and Society* (Weber 1922): the early study, published as two journal essays in 1904–05, that reads the historical emergence of modern capitalism as constitutively shaped by an ascetic-Protestant orientation toward worldly work — work as calling, methodical accumulation as evidence of election, the inner-worldly asceticism that produced both the rationalized work-discipline and the systematic accumulation that capital required. The argument grounds Weber's broader thesis about *Wertrationalität* and *Zweckrationalität* and is one of the founding texts of the sociology of religion as well as economic sociology.

This is a pending reference stub: the work has not yet been directly read for this library. Expected citation roles: foundational citation for the sociology of work, for [`marxism/theories/political-economy/`](../../../triage/theories/critical-theory/theories/marxism/theories/political-economy) when the Marx–Weber dialogue on capitalism is engaged, and for the broader concept of *rationalization* as it propagates through the [`foucauldian/`](../../../triage/theories/critical-theory/theories/foucauldian) and [`han/`](../../../triage/theories/critical-theory/theories/han) subdomains.
